Computer Architecture Foundations & System Buses

Von Neumann vs Harvard Architecture Foundation

The structural paradigm of how processors interact with memory:

FeatureVon Neumann ArchitectureHarvard Architecture
Memory SpaceUnified memory (shared data & instructions)Separate physical memories for code & data
Bus StructureSingle shared bus (Data + Instruction)Independent instruction and data buses
BottleneckVon Neumann Bottleneck (cannot read code and data simultaneously)No bus conflict; dual concurrent fetches
Modern UsageMain PC RAM & System ArchitectureL1 CPU Caches (L1-I and L1-D), DSPs, Microcontrollers
Modern Hybrid Model: Desktop/Server CPUs (Intel/AMD/ARM) operate as Modified Harvard: Unified external RAM, but separate internal L1 Instruction and L1 Data caches.
The Three System Buses Interconnect
┌────────────────┐ Control Bus (Read/Write/Ready/Interrupts) │ │ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════► Memory & I/O │ Central │ Address Bus (Unidirectional: Memory Addresses) │ Processing │ ───────────────────────────────────────────────► Decoders │ Unit (CPU) │ Data Bus (Bidirectional: 64-bit Payload) │ │ ◄─────────────────────────────────────────────► Data Buffers └────────────────┘
  • Address Bus: Unidirectional. Width defines max addressable physical RAM ($2^N$). A 32-bit bus addresses $2^{32} = 4\text{ GB}$; a 48-bit physical address bus addresses $2^{48} = 256\text{ TB}$.
  • Data Bus: Bidirectional. Carries actual data and instructions. Width defines word size transfer per cycle (64 bits = 8 bytes per transfer in modern CPUs).
  • Control Bus: Coordinates timing and direction signals (MEMR, MEMW, IOR, IOW, clock, bus requests, and hardware interrupts).
02

Central Processing Unit (CPU) Microarchitecture

Core Execution Engine Silicon
  • ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit): Computes integer arithmetic (+, -, *) and boolean logic (AND, OR, XOR).
  • FPU / Vector Unit: Floating Point Unit (IEEE 754) & SIMD engines (AVX2, AVX-512).
  • Control Unit (CU): Decodes opcodes, manages execution micro-ops, directs data paths.
  • Registers: Fastest on-chip storage (<1 cycle). General Purpose, Program Counter (PC/IP), Stack Pointer (SP), Flags/Status.
Instruction Pipeline & Hazards Pipelining
[IF: Fetch] ──► [ID: Decode] ──► [EX: Execute] ▲ │ Branch Prediction ▼ [WB: Writeback] ◄── [MEM: Memory Access]
  • Structural Hazard: Hardware resource conflict.
  • Data Hazard (RAW/WAR/WAW): Instruction depends on previous result (solved by Forwarding / Out-of-Order).
  • Control Hazard: Branch jumps (mitigated by Branch Predictors & Speculation).
ISA: x86-64 vs ARM64 Architecture
Parameterx86-64 (CISC)ARM64 (RISC)
Instruction LengthVariable (1–15 bytes)Fixed (32 bits / 4 bytes)
Design PhilosophyComplex operations, legacy compatibilityLoad/Store, simplified instructions
Power ProfileHigher power, high peak single-coreHigh power efficiency (perf/watt)
Dominant SpaceDesktops, High-End ServersMobile, Apple M-series, AWS Graviton

04

Primary Memory Architecture: RAM & ROM Technologies

DRAM vs SRAM & DDR Generations RAM
  • SRAM (Static RAM): 6 transistors per cell (flip-flop). No refresh cycle needed. Ultra-low latency, low density, high cost. Used in CPU caches.
  • DRAM (Dynamic RAM): 1 transistor + 1 capacitor (1T-1C). Capacitor leaks charge; requires periodic electrical refresh (~every 64 ms). High density, used for main RAM.
FeatureDDR4DDR5
Standard Data Rates2133 – 3200 MT/s4800 – 8400+ MT/s
Operating Voltage1.2V1.1V (on-module PMIC)
Channel ArchitectureSingle 64-bit channel / DIMMDual 32-bit subchannels / DIMM
Error CorrectionSideband ECC (Server only)On-Die ECC (Standard) + Sideband
Burst LengthBL8BL16 (Double prefetch)
Memory Timings, Multi-Channel & Virtual Memory Performance

Latency & Timings (e.g., CL16-18-18-38):

  • CAS Latency (CL): Number of clock cycles between memory controller issuing read request and first data bit output. Absolute latency: $t = \frac{\text{CL} \times 2000}{\text{Data Rate (MT/s)}}$ ns.
  • Multi-Channel Architecture: Dual-channel doubles bus width from 64-bit to 128-bit, effectively doubling theoretical maximum peak bandwidth: $$\text{Bandwidth (MB/s)} = \text{Clock (MHz)} \times 8 \text{ bytes} \times \text{Channels}$$
MMU & Virtual Memory: Hardware Memory Management Unit (MMU) translates virtual addresses to physical RAM via Page Tables (4 KB standard pages). The TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) caches recent address mappings to prevent costly multi-level page table walks.

Secondary Storage: Magnetic HDDs vs Solid-State Drives

Figure 4: Physical Internal Comparison: Mechanical HDD (Spinning Magnetic Platter, Spindle, Voice-Coil Actuator Arm & Read/Write Head) vs. M.2 NVMe SSD (Flash Controller Microchip, DRAM Cache & 3D NAND Silicon Chips)
Hard Disk Drives (HDD) Magnetic
  • Mechanical Components: Rotating magnetic platters, spindle motor (5400 / 7200 RPM), voice-coil actuator arm with read/write heads.
  • Access Latency: Seek time (3–10 ms) + Rotational latency (4.16 ms @ 7200 RPM).
  • Recording: CMR (Conventional) vs SMR (Shingled - overlapping tracks, slower rewrite speeds).
  • Use Case: Bulk cold storage & NAS archives.

06

Graphics Processing Units (GPU) & Hardware Accelerators

CPU vs GPU Architecture Paradigms Compute

Architectural design trade-offs: Latency Optimization vs Throughput Maximization:

CPU: Low Latency / Heavy Cores GPU: Massive Parallel SIMT Throughput ┌───────────────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Large Cache (L3 32-96MB) │ │ Small Cache │ ├─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────┤ │ [C][C][C][C][C][C][C][C][C][C][C][C] │ │ Core 0 │ Core 1 │ Core 2 │ ... │ │ [C][C][C][C] Thousands of Stream Cores │ │ +Out-of-│ +Branch │ +Huge │ │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Order │ Pred │ ALUs │ │ │ Ultra-Wide Memory Bus (128 - 384 bit) │ └─────────┴─────────┴─────────┴─────┘ │ High Bandwidth VRAM (GDDR6 / HBM3) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • CPU: Optimized for sequential code execution, branch-heavy logic, ultra-low single-thread latency.
  • GPU: SIMT (Single Instruction Multiple Threads). Executes identical instructions concurrently across massive matrices of vertices, pixels, or tensor weights.
Dedicated Processing Cores & VRAM Acceleration
  • Shader / CUDA / Stream Cores: Standard FP32 & INT32 programmable arithmetic pipelines for 3D rasterization and physics.
  • Ray Tracing (RT) Cores: Dedicated silicon hardware designed to compute Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) ray-triangle box intersections for photorealistic lighting and reflections.
  • Tensor / Matrix Cores: Specialized low-precision matrix multiply-accumulate engines (FP16, BF16, INT8, FP8) driving deep learning and AI inferences (DLSS, LLM inference).
  • VRAM (Video Memory):
    • GDDR6 / GDDR6X: High-frequency discrete graphics memory operating across 128-bit to 384-bit buses (up to 1,000+ GB/s).
    • HBM (High Bandwidth Memory): 3D-stacked silicon dies connected via silicon interposer directly adjacent to the GPU die (up to 3,000+ GB/s in datacenter GPUs like NVIDIA H100).

Power Supply Units (PSU) & Thermal Dissipation

Power Delivery & 80 PLUS Standards Power

Converts high-voltage alternating current (110V/230V AC) to regulated DC power rails:

  • +12V Rail: Primary power rail for high-draw hardware (CPU & GPU).
  • +5V & +3.3V Rails: Powers motherboard logic, M.2 drives, USB devices.
  • +5VSB (Standby): Keeps motherboard listening for power button / WoL.
80 PLUS Rating50% Load Efficiency100% Load Efficiency
80 PLUS Bronze85%81%
80 PLUS Gold90%87%
80 PLUS Platinum92%89%
80 PLUS Titanium94%90%
ATX 3.0 & 12V-2x6 Connector: Supplies up to 600W through a single cable with sideband sense pins to prevent catastrophic GPU power-spike shutdowns.
Thermodynamics & Cooling Physics Thermal

Cooling moves heat from die through three thermodynamic mechanisms:

[Silicon Die] ──► [TIM / Thermal Paste] ──► [Copper Baseplate] │ (Phase-change liquid vaporization) ▼ [Finned Heatsink Aluminum] ◄── [Sintered Copper Heatpipes] │ (Forced air convection via PWM Fans) ▼ [Ambient Exhaust Air Out]
  • Air Cooler: Heatpipes filled with low-pressure liquid vaporize heat to aluminum fin stacks. Reliable, zero pump failure risk.
  • AIO Liquid Cooler: Micro-channel copper pump block cycles liquid coolant to external radiator. Higher thermal buffer capacity.
  • Thermal Throttling: CPU/GPU automatically drops multiplier clocks once hitting maximum thermal junction ($T_j \text{Max} \approx 95^\circ\text{C}-100^\circ\text{C}$) to prevent hardware damage.

Hardware Diagnostic & POST Flowchart Diagnostics

When powering on a machine, the motherboard initiates POST (Power-On Self-Test):

1. Press Power Button ──► PSU Power-Good (+12V stable) │ 2. [CPU LED / Code 00-15] ──► Detects CPU & microcode │ (If hangs: Check 8-pin CPU EPS power, bent socket pins) 3. [DRAM LED / Code 16-55] ──► Memory Training & SPD check │ (If hangs: Reseat RAM, test single DIMM in slot A2, clear CMOS) 4. [VGA LED / Code 60-99] ──► Initializes GPU & display output │ (If hangs: Reseat PCIe card, check PCIe auxiliary 8-pin cables) 5. [BOOT LED / Code A0-A9] ──► Bootloader handoff to NVMe/SATA │ (If hangs: UEFI boot order, partition table MBR vs GPT mismatch) 6. OS Kernel loads successfully!
Bottleneck Diagnosis: If GPU runs at 99-100% and CPU at 40%, system is GPU-bound (ideal for gaming). If CPU hits 100% while GPU hovers at 50-70%, system is CPU-bound (CPU cannot feed frame draw calls fast enough).
